//: CSS linting, whose ONE load-bearing rule is declaration-strict-value: no
colour may be written outside tokens.css.
WHY IT EXISTS. tokens.css opens with 'Do not add colours outside this
file.' That rule has been stated since the design system was written and
enforced by nothing — JS and TSX are linted with oxlint and
--deny-warnings, while ~5,500 lines of design-system CSS plus feature CSS
had no automated guard at all. A raw hex added in a feature module is
invisible to review until somebody notices the theme is wrong in one place,
and it defeats light/dark switching entirely because a literal cannot vary
by theme.
WHY stylelint-config-standard IS NOT EXTENDED. It brings roughly forty
stylistic rules that would fail across 110 existing files on introduction,
and fixing them is a formatting change dressed up as a lint adoption. The
cost is that this configuration is small; the benefit is that its one rule
means something. Additional rules are worth adopting one at a time, each
with its own reason.
WHICH PROPERTIES, AND WHY box-shadow IS ABSENT. '/color$/' covers color,
background-color, border-color, outline-color and the rest by suffix; fill
and stroke are the SVG equivalents. box-shadow was in the first version and
was removed after measuring: its value is composite — offsets, blur, spread,
THEN a colour — so a whole-value check can never match '^var(--' even when
the colour is a token. It flagged 'inset 3px 0 0 var(--acc)' and
'inset var(--bar-w) 0 0 0 var(--acc)', both perfectly tokenised. A rule that
fires on correct code teaches people to disable it. The cost is stated
rather than hidden: a genuine 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.18)' inside a box-shadow is
still unlinted and is left to review.
WHY color-mix() IS IGNORED. Its ARGUMENTS carry the colour, and in every
current use they are tokens — 'color-mix(in srgb, var(--cyn) 60%,
var(--line))'. The rule compares whole values, so without the exception the
correct tokenised form is rejected. The looseness is real: 'color-mix(in
srgb, #fff 50%, red)' would pass. It is accepted because the alternative
rejects the idiom the design system uses in 32 files.

scale-unlimited/declaration-strict-value.message: Use a design token — var(--…) — rather than a literal colour. Colours are defined in src/styles/tokens.css and nowhere else.

//overrides: tokens.css is where the literals live, so the rule cannot apply to it.
fonts.css carries @font-face url() references and no colour.
src/premium/** is a reference-only parallel prototype application with its
own provisional brand, pinned as unreachable from the production entry by
